post_ship_review.scope: full-collection rescan + adversarial re-audit (Codex GPT-5.6-sol + independent Claude cross-check), applied via ZH source of truth
post_ship_review.fix: 2026-07-12 full-collection rescan: Codex GPT-5.6-sol flagged 15 candidate errors on the ZH source, an independent Claude thread adversarially tried to refute each one → 11 CONFIRMED + 3 NEEDS_NUANCE fixed, 1 REFUTED left as-is. Summary of fixes carried over to this EN edition: (1) reworded the CoT 'latent space' phrasing to 'reasons within its own token sequence' (TL;DR + Q1) — the real CoT-vs-ReAct distinction is external grounding, not latent-vs-explicit; (2) tightened POMDP terminology in §1.1 to distinguish hidden state s_t / history h_t (a sufficient statistic) / belief b_t (the minimal sufficient statistic), and aligned the §1.3 state row with it; (3) separated Plan-and-Solve (Wang 2023, single-generation prompting only, no tool calls) from the production Plan-and-Execute architecture (a later tool-calling + replanning engineering pattern), so the latter's content is no longer misattributed to the Wang 2023 paper (TL;DR + §3.1); (4) de-absolutized function-calling schema compliance: plain function calling does not guarantee 100% compliance, only strict/Structured Outputs (2024-08 onward) does; added OpenAI's own gpt-4-0613 35.4% compliance figure (§5.1 table + §5.3 + Q5); (5) clarified the §5.3 JSON example as Anthropic-specific field names (input_schema/tool_use/input), noting OpenAI's equivalents (parameters/tool_calls/function.arguments); (6) corrected MCP's standardization layer from transport to application layer (JSON-RPC message schema + capability negotiation, end of §5.1); (7) de-misleadingified the stdio security model: the child process inherits the full privileges of the host user with no extra sandbox; its relative safety comes from no public exposure, not an OS-enforced boundary (§6.1.4); (8) clarified that MCP's prompt-injection trust boundary lives entirely at the host-application layer, consistent with the already-accurate wording in Q13 (§6.1.4); (9) fixed the self-contradictory 'prepend to the end' in the §7.3 working-memory mitigation to 'prepend to the beginning'; (10) added the i.i.d. precondition to the §9.3 Pass@k formula (agent retries are often correlated, so real reliability gains are lower than the formula implies), mirrored in Q19; (11) fixed Q6's 'AlfWorld 75 → 97' to '75/134 (~56%) → 130/134 (~97%)', avoiding mixing a raw count with a percentage; (12) softened Q18's 'Verified sampling ensures both are clean' to 'aims to filter out the most obvious cases', removing the self-contradiction with the same answer's later '~59% still flawed' statement; (13) separated Q24's DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI o-series rule-based-reward claims — R1 is confirmed, o-series remains unconfirmed community inference; (14) reworded Q25's 'Human upper bound' to 'Human reference score', citing the already-present §8.3 fact that Simular crossed the OSWorld human baseline at 72.6% on 2025-12-16, so the baseline is not implied to be uncrossable. The REFUTED item was left unchanged: L444's 'HTTPS POST + SSE bidirectional stream' phrasing was verified to mean POST (client→server) + SSE (server→client) together forming the bidirectional stream, not a claim that SSE itself is bidirectional — not an error. This EN edition was updated with natural-English equivalents of every fix above, matching the ZH source of truth line-for-line; both editions were re-rendered and their sidecar hashes refreshed.
